name: The Cedar House
kicker: A nine-room machiya conversion in Nakagyo
overview: A restored merchant townhouse of nine rooms arranged around two courtyard gardens, five minutes' walk from Nishiki market. The conversion keeps the original cedar structure and the tsuboniwa gardens, and adds underfloor heating, deep cypress baths and a small breakfast room that opens onto the inner court.
location: Nakagyo ward, central Kyoto — walking distance to Nishiki market, Pontocho and the Kamo river.
whyStayHere: The machiya form is the reason to stay in Kyoto rather than any other Japanese city, and there are very few conversions of this quality left in the centre.

name: Nongriat Forest Guesthouse
kicker: Simple rooms beside the root bridges
overview: Six simple rooms in Nongriat village, reachable only on foot down roughly three thousand steps, beside the double-decker living root bridge. There is no road, no vehicle noise, and the river pools are a two-minute walk away.
location: Nongriat village, East Khasi Hills — a 3,000-step descent from Tyrna, no road access.
whyStayHere: Staying overnight means having the root bridges to yourself in the early morning and evening.
The descent and ascent are far more enjoyable split across two days.
The river pools below the village are extraordinary and almost empty at dawn.
Village-run, with the money staying in Nongriat.
bestRooms: The two rooms facing the forest.
All rooms are simple — expect a bed, a fan and a shared or basic private bathroom.
bestFor: Anyone prioritising the experience over comfort
notFor: Travellers with mobility limitations — there is no road
Anyone needing air conditioning or reliable power
bestTime: October to April. Steps are dangerously slippery in monsoon.
pros: Root bridges at dawn with nobody there
considerations: 3,000 steps each way, carrying your own bag or hiring a porter
Leeches and slippery steps in the wet months
